one_month_reasoning: The Q3 2026 report on 22 Oct 2026 falls inside the window (Nokia release; source 6). Consensus (Infront, 4 Aug) expects Q3 net sales EUR 5,051m, comparable operating profit EUR 444m (8.8% margin) and comparable EPS EUR 0.06 (0.04-0.07); management guided Mobile Infrastructure gross margin down to 44-46% in Q3 from 49.3% and FCF conversion toward the low end of 55-75%. Nokia beat on profit in Q2 (EUR 434m vs ~EUR 382m consensus) yet fell 5.35% to $9.73 on supply/memory and legacy worries (source 18), so a beat is not enough; the stock reacts to AI & Cloud orders and the 2026 guide (currently EUR 2.1-2.6bn, 'somewhat above the midpoint'). The stock is also up ~6.2-6.5% today after rising from the July low, which slightly favours short-term giveback. Net: median ~$10.78 (just under today's ~$10.84), log-sd 0.175 = 62%/3.5 monthly vol, fat enough for a +/-8-10% earnings-day move; no directional earnings call.

fair_value.method: Blend of 21x Oct-2027 NTM comparable EPS of EUR 0.445 (=EUR 9.35 = $10.54 at EUR/USD 1.1269), weight 0.65, and a FCF DCF from S&P's EUR 1.6bn 2028 FCF at 9% WACC/3% terminal (=EUR 6.02 = $6.79), weight 0.35; 0.65x10.54 + 0.35x6.79 = $9.23 (EUR 8.19).

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Oct-2027 NTM EPS EUR 0.445 (FY27 consensus 0.408, FY28 +12%) x 21x = EUR 9.35 x 1.1269 = $10.54

inputs_detail.derivation: StockAnalysis (S&P Global) FY2027 EPS EUR 0.40844 (+19.1% on FY2026 EUR 0.343); cross-check Yahoo FY2027 avg 0.48 USD-quoted (=EUR 0.426 at 1.1269), range 0.38-0.60.
Infront consensus compiled by Nokia, 4 Aug 2026; 2026 comparable operating profit EUR 2,400m.

Below the +19.1% consensus 2026->27 step: S&P projects Network Infrastructure growth of 10-15% for 2026-27 while ~73% of sales (Telecommunication Providers EUR 3,514m of 4,815m in Q2) grew ~3%; mgmt says AI-RAN only commercial toward end-2027 with volume in 2028. 0.40844 x 1.12 = 0.4575.

12-peer forward P/E median 24.4x (range 14.7-51.8x); telecom-equipment subgroup (ERIC, ZTE, CSCO, HPE, CALX, ADTN) median 18.7x; optical/AI subgroup (CIEN, ANET, LITE, COHR, GLW, FN) median 42.4x. Nokia's Q2 operating profit was 65% Mobile Infrastructure (EUR 310m) vs 35% Network Infrastructure (EUR 166m), so a profit-weighted blend is ~27x on today's peak-cycle optical multiples; 21x (inside range, below median) haircuts that for multiple normalisation by Oct 2027 and Nokia's weak cash conversion (FCF tracking low end of 55-75%).
ECB reference rate 6 Oct 2026 (Twelve Data spot 1.12605 cross-check); ADR = 1 ordinary share: StockAnalysis market cap $57.54B / 5.60B shares = $10.27/share, in line with the ADR price, i.e. 1:1.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: FCF 2028 EUR 1.6bn (S&P), +8%/yr to 2032, WACC 9%, g 3%, net cash EUR 2.78bn, 5.802bn diluted shares, EUR/USD 1.1269

inputs_detail.derivation: S&P (Aug 2026) projects FCF after leases of ~EUR 1.1bn in 2026 rising to EUR 1.6bn in 2028; used as first explicit year after Oct 2027.
Between S&P's 10-15% Network Infrastructure growth and flat-to-low-single-digit telecom-provider sales (+3% y/y in Q2: 3,514 vs 3,408).

StockAnalysis shows a WACC of 8.21% for NOK and 6.6%-15.3% for peers (e.g. ERIC 6.57%, CSCO 9.33%, HPE 10.66%); 9% adds a premium for 62% realized volatility and the AI-order cyclicality vs NOK's 0.77 beta.
Nominal GDP-like growth for a mature network-equipment franchise.
Net cash and interest-bearing financial investments at 30 Jun 2026; held flat to Oct 2027 (FCF ~ offsets dividends EUR 0.04/qtr and restructuring cash).
Q2 2026 average diluted shares 5,801,886k (total shares 5,742,239,696 less 83,304,077 treasury = 5,658.9m basic).
PV(FCF 2028-32 at 9%, mid-year from Oct 2027) EUR 7.36bn + PV(TV = 2.177 x 1.03 / 0.06 = 37.37bn) EUR 24.82bn + net cash 2.78bn = 34.95bn; /5.802bn sh = EUR 6.02 x 1.1269 = USD 6.79.

bear.story: AI & Cloud orders (EUR 2.8bn in Q2, only ~half converting within 12 months) prove partly double-ordered or delayed by memory/silicon shortages; Mobile Infrastructure margin reverts (Q3 GM guided 44-46%), legacy telco spend stays flat, FCF stays near the low end of conversion. Consensus EPS gets cut ~15-20% -> NTM EPS ~EUR 0.36 at a telecom-equipment multiple of 17x (ERIC/CALX/ZTE zone) = EUR 6.12 = $6.90.

base.story: Nokia delivers roughly consensus (2026 comp. op. profit ~EUR 2.4bn, 2027 EPS ~EUR 0.41) with optical/IP growth offset by a flat telco base; the market keeps paying a below-median 21x on NTM EPS EUR 0.445 as optical-peer multiples normalise = $10.54, about flat vs today.

bull.story: AI & Cloud keeps doubling, the InP/optical capacity expansion converts orders faster, AI-RAN/defense add optionality, and Mobile Infrastructure margins hold: NTM EPS ~EUR 0.52 at 28x (between peer median 24x and optical subgroup 42x) = $16.41, near the June peak.

comps_summary.peer_range: Forward P/E 14.7x (HPE) to 51.8x (LITE), median 24.4x; telecom-equipment subgroup median 18.7x, optical/AI subgroup median 42.4x. EV/EBITDA shown is TRAILING (forward EV/EBITDA not freely available): 7.8x (ADTN) to 123.9x (LITE), median 28.3x; NOK 18.7x TTM, 24.0x forward P/E today.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 21x NTM P/E applied to Oct-2027 NTM EPS: inside the range, ~14% below the 12-peer median and ~2x above the telecom subgroup median; NOK today trades at 24.0x forward, i.e. at the median.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: Discount to the full-peer median, not a premium: (1) mix - 73% of Q2 sales (EUR 3,514m of 4,815m) came from Telecommunication Providers growing ~3% y/y and Q2 operating profit was 65% Mobile Infrastructure, so most earnings belong in the 15-22x telecom-equipment group, while AI & Cloud is only 9% of sales; (2) cash conversion - FCF guided to the low end of 55-75% of comparable profit and S&P sees FCF of only ~EUR 1.1bn in 2026 vs ~EUR 2.0bn comparable net profit, with EUR 800m of 2026 restructuring charges excluded from 'comparable' earnings; (3) the optical subgroup's 35-52x multiples embed 50-65% next-year EPS growth vs Nokia's +19%. These are structural features of Nokia's portfolio that will persist through the horizon, so the discount is not a sell-side 'underperform' call.

thesis_break_reason: A close below ~$7.00 (EUR ~6.2, ~15x FY2027 consensus EPS, 28% below the July post-Q2 low of $9.73) would most likely mean the AI & Cloud order book is unwinding (double ordering/cancellations) or 2026-27 guidance is cut, i.e. the earnings base itself is wrong rather than ordinary 62%-vol noise; at that point the bear scenario becomes the base.

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 results: consensus comp. op. profit EUR 444m, EPS EUR 0.06; AI & Cloud orders, Mobile Infra GM (guided 44-46%), FCF vs low-end conversion
Restructuring: EUR 800m 2026 charges; Q4 cash outflows and workforce reductions
Q4 2026 results and first FY2027 outlook
Q2 2027 results: test of whether H1-2026 AI & Cloud orders converted (~half within 12 months per CEO)
AI-RAN (Nvidia) trials in 2027, commercial availability toward end-2027 per CEO; volume 2028
Memory / leading-edge silicon supply constraints (CEO: 'clearly constraints there'); FX - EUR/USD moves translate directly into the ADR price
Possible S&P upgrade (BBB- positive) or Moody's move to investment grade (Ba1 positive)

key_uncertainties: Durability and conversion of AI & Cloud orders (EUR 2.8bn in Q2; Bernstein raised double-ordering risk on the call)
Profitability of mobile networks ex-licensing: Light Reading questions whether radio + core software are loss-making once ~70%-margin licensing is stripped out of Mobile Infrastructure
Cash conversion: Q2 FCF was -EUR 732m, guidance at the low end of 55-75%, EUR 800m 2026 restructuring charges
Whether optical-peer multiples (35-52x) persist or compress by Oct 2027
EUR/USD: the ADR is a USD translation of a EUR stock; a 5% EUR move is ~5% on the ADR

Defense exposure is not separately disclosed: 'Mission Critical Enterprise & Defense' customers were EUR 448m in Q2 2026 (9.3% of sales, -3% y/y reported) and EUR 914m in H1 (9.9%); defense products (5G tactical radio, mission-safe phone) and NATO spending are optionality, not a reported revenue line
reasoning: Facts: NOK $10.84 (~EUR 9.62 at ECB EUR/USD 1.1269, 6 Oct 2026), 5.80bn diluted shares -> market cap ~EUR 55.8bn, net cash EUR 2.78bn, EV ~EUR 53bn. Trading 28.3x FY2026 consensus comp. EPS EUR 0.34 and 23.6x FY2027 EUR 0.408. Bear-lane findings: (a) no short-seller report, short interest only ~1% of float, no insider selling - the CEO bought 84,404 shares at EUR 9.15 in April; (b) credit is not the problem: S&P BBB- and Moody's Ba1 both on positive outlook, net cash; litigation is mostly Nokia as SEP plaintiff (wins vs Acer/Asus), a lumpiness rather than solvency risk; (c) the real bear points are earnings quality and valuation: 'comparable' excludes EUR 390m of Q2 restructuring (reported diluted EPS EUR 0.00 vs comparable 0.07; EUR 800m charges in 2026), Q2 FCF -EUR 732m and FY conversion at the low end of 55-75%, S&P's FCF of ~EUR 1.1bn (2026) is a ~2% FCF yield; trailing P/FCF ~96x; AI & Cloud is ~9% of sales while 73% is telco customers growing ~3%; Light Reading questions mobile networks' underlying profitability; Santander (Underperform, EUR 6.85) and Danske/DNB Carnegie (Hold) downgrades earlier in 2026 and Bernstein's double-ordering question. The stock already round-tripped from $17.45 (June) to $9.73 (July) on these issues, so part of the bear case is priced. Valuation: P/E (21x NTM EUR 0.445 = $10.54) and DCF ($6.79) blend to $9.23, ~15% below spot. Scenarios bear $6.90 (30%) / base $10.54 (50%) / bull $16.41 (20%), probability-weighted ~$10.6; the ladder is a mixture of lognormals around those (log-sd 0.30-0.33 each, total ~0.43, below 62% realized vol which was inflated by the June spike-and-crash) giving a median ~$10.15 and P(>=10.84) = 0.44. Research limits: nokia.com newsroom pages returned 403 (used the EDGAR 6-K and the consensus PDF), sec.gov refused scripted access (used WebFetch), Twelve Data/Alpha Vantage estimates and statistics endpoints were plan-gated, forward EV/EBITDA for peers not freely available (TTM shown). Source mix: 11 of the 21 non-comps sources are bear-lane (credit, downgrades, critical journalism, insider, litigation, Substack); the 24 peer-data pages required by the comps rule push the overall in-lane share below 60%.
